newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan, HK reach shipping link agreement.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan, HK reach shipping link agreement.

text.p: Taiwan and Hong Kong on Saturday resolved differences over a controversial flag issue, agreeing to continue a direct shipping link after the July 1 handover of the British colony to China.
After more than six hours of talks, the sides signed a memorandum which would allow their ships to enter each other's ports after July 1, negotiators said in a news briefing.
Hong Kong chief negotiator George Chao said the agreement was reached after the two sides temporarily resolved the flag issue.
"Hong Kong is a special administrative region. We will fly the bauhinia flag. And because you (Taiwan) don't have such (identification) flag, Taiwan temporarily would not fly the flag," he said.
Under the agreement, both sides would do away with the sensitive national flags.
The sides had been unable to overcome the flag question during a first round of talks in Hong Kong on May 2.
The accord clears the way for a much-needed shipping link which could otherwise have been suspended at midnight on June 30 when Hong Kong is handed back to China by Britain.
